title: Donyati Expert Agents — Plugin Usage Guide
subtitle: Setup and usage in Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and claude.ai web
header_text: Donyati Expert Agents — Plugin Usage Guide v2.4.1

content.text: The plugin connects Claude (Code, Desktop, or web) to Donyati's Expert Agents platform (expert-agents.donyati.com), and the same platform is reachable from ChatGPT through a connector. You get expert consultations, multi-agent comparisons, document summarization, knowledge search, and identity verification — same backend across all three surfaces.

items: Expert consultations — ask any of 26+ platform specialists a question
Multi-agent comparisons — get unbiased platform comparisons (e.g. Snowflake vs Databricks)
Document summarization — domain-aware summaries of proposals, SOWs, transcripts
Knowledge search — pull verified citations from Donyati's curated knowledge base
Identity verification — confirm your access before relying on it

content.title: Works in four places
content.text: Donyati Expert Agents runs in Claude Code (full plugin with /donyati-* slash commands, requires an API key), Claude Desktop and claude.ai web (Custom Connector + Donyati SSO), and ChatGPT (connector + SSO). Same backend, same answers, same access rules. On ChatGPT everything works except the /donyati-* slash commands, which are MCP prompts that Claude surfaces and ChatGPT does not — you ask in plain English instead. Setup is section 3C.
What you need depends on which client you're using:

rows: Claude Code CLI (claude.com/claude-code), Terminal, and an API key from Matt (mjanecek@donyati.com)
Claude Desktop app (claude.ai/download), Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan, your Donyati Azure AD login
A browser, Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan, your Donyati Azure AD login
A ChatGPT plan that allows custom connectors, your Donyati Azure AD login

content.title: Connector users don't need an API key
content.text: You authenticate with your normal Donyati Microsoft 365 / Azure AD account when you add the connector. Claude Code is the only surface that uses the dea_* key system.

If you're on Claude Code and don't have a key yet, request one from Matt with your name (used to label the key in admin logs) and the team you're on (Sales / Presales / Marketing / CS) for usage attribution. You'll typically receive the key back within a few hours.

You'll run one command in Terminal (to save your key) and two commands inside Claude Code (to install the plugin). That's it — no git, no cloning, no path hunting. Using Claude Desktop or claude.ai web instead? Skip to Section 3B.
Step 1 — Save your key (Terminal)
Open Terminal and paste this one line (replace dea_paste_your_key_here with the actual key Matt sent you), then press Enter. Linux/WSL users: replace ~/.zshrc with ~/.bashrc in both spots.

content.title: Paste into Terminal
content.text: echo 'export DONYATI_API_KEY="dea_paste_your_key_here"' >> ~/.zshrc && source ~/.zshrc

content.title: Straight quotes only
content.text: When you paste, make sure the quotes are straight ("), not curly. Email clients and Slack sometimes convert them. Curly quotes are the most common cause of 401 errors after install.
To confirm the key stuck, type: echo $DONYATI_API_KEY — you should see your key printed back.
Step 2 — Install the plugin (inside Claude Code)
Open Claude Code (type "claude" in Terminal, or use whatever method you normally do). Type these two slash commands, one at a time:

content.title: Command 1 — add the marketplace
content.text: /plugin marketplace add matt-janecek/consulting-agents
Claude Code clones the marketplace internally. You don't need to know git or have a GitHub login — Claude Code handles it.

content.title: Command 2 — install the plugin
content.text: /plugin install donyati-expert-agents@donyati-plugins
This registers all 7 slash commands and the MCP connection to the Expert Agents server in one shot.
Step 3 — Verify

Still inside Claude Code, run /donyati-setup. You should see your key name, owner email, key ID, scopes, and rate limit. If you see that, you're done — try /donyati-help to see everything. If you see an error, jump to Section 7 (Troubleshooting).
Never used Terminal before?
That's fine — here's the minimum you need:

rows: Search "WSL" or "Git Bash" in Start menu

content.text: That's all you need for this guide. If you get stuck at any step, screenshot the error and send to Matt.
Two steps, no terminal, no API key. Authentication is your normal Donyati Microsoft 365 / Azure AD login — same SSO popup you use everywhere else.
Step 1 — Add the Custom Connector (Claude Desktop)

items: Open Claude Desktop, then Settings (⌘+, on Mac) → Connectors.
Click "Add custom connector" — you may need to expand the Advanced section.
Name: Donyati Expert Agents

content.text: Step 1 — Add the Custom Connector (claude.ai web)

items: Go to https://claude.ai → click your profile → Settings → Connectors.
Scroll to Custom Connectors → Add custom connector.
Use the same Name and URL as the Desktop steps above.
Click Add.

content.text: Step 2 — Sign in with Azure AD

content.title: Your SSO session is the authentication
content.text: When you click Add/Connect, a Microsoft sign-in popup opens. Use your Donyati Microsoft 365 account — the same one you use for Outlook, Teams, and the Expert Agents web app. Approve the popup. The connector shows ~8 tools as available. There's no API key field, no Authorization header, no Bearer token to paste.
Step 3 — Verify

content.title: Prompt to test the connection
content.text: Start a new Claude conversation and type: "Use the Donyati whoami tool to confirm my access." Claude calls the whoami tool and reports your name, email, and scopes. If you see that, you're done.
How to use the tools without slash commands
Just describe what you want and mention "Donyati" or the tool name. Claude picks the right tool. Translation table:

rows: /donyati-ask How do you handle IC eliminations in OneStream?
Ask the Donyati OneStream expert how they handle intercompany eliminations.
Use Donyati to compare Snowflake and Databricks for AI/ML workloads.
Summarize this SOW using the Donyati summarize tool. (paste content)
Search Donyati's knowledge base for predictive forecasting articles.
Use the Donyati whoami tool to confirm my access.

content.text: All workflow examples in Section 5 work identically on Desktop/web — just phrase the request in plain English instead of slashes.
Desktop / web troubleshooting

items: "Couldn't reach the MCP server" when adding the connector — typically a typo in the URL. Confirm it's exactly https://expert-agents.donyati.com/api/mcp (note /api/mcp at the end).
Microsoft sign-in popup blocked — unblock popups for claude.ai (web) or for the Claude Desktop app. The connector relies on a popup for SSO.
"Unauthorized" / Azure AD error after sign-in — your Microsoft account isn't in Donyati's tenant. Sign in with your @donyati.com Microsoft account, not a personal one.
No "Custom Connectors" option visible — your Claude plan doesn't include it. Upgrade to Pro / Max / Team / Enterprise, or fall back to Claude Code (any plan).

Tools appear but every call returns an error — the OAuth access token may have expired (24 h lifetime). Open the connector settings and reconnect — the SSO refresh is silent if you're already signed into Microsoft elsewhere.

content.text: Same connector as Claude Desktop, same sign-in, no API key. One thing differs and it is worth knowing before you start: ChatGPT does not show the /donyati-* slash commands. Every command is still available to you as a tool — you ask for it in plain English.

items: In ChatGPT, open Settings → Connectors. On some plans this sits under a Developer mode or Advanced toggle; the exact location moves between releases and plans.
Choose to add a custom connector / MCP server.

content.text: If you cannot find a way to add a custom connector at all, your ChatGPT plan or your workspace admin does not allow them. That is a ChatGPT-side setting rather than anything Donyati controls — Claude Code works on any plan if you need a fallback.
Step 2 — Sign in with Azure AD

content.title: Your SSO session is the authentication
content.text: A Microsoft sign-in opens. Use your Donyati Microsoft 365 account — the same one you use for Outlook, Teams, and the Expert Agents web app. Approve it. There is no API key field and no token to paste.
Step 3 — Verify
In a new chat, say: “Use the Donyati whoami tool to confirm my access.” You should get back your name, email, and active scopes. If that works, you are done.

content.title: Name the client and the project
content.text: The slash commands look the client up for you; in plain English you should say it — “using Acme's FCC project” — so the answer is grounded in that engagement's knowledge instead of being a generic platform answer.
ChatGPT troubleshooting

items: No way to add a custom connector — your plan or workspace admin does not allow them. Nothing to fix on the Donyati side.
“Couldn't reach the server” — check the URL is exactly https://expert-agents.donyati.com/api/mcp, including /api/mcp.
“Unauthorized” after sign-in — you signed in with a personal Microsoft account. Use your @donyati.com one.

You cannot see a client you expect — access is your own, by Microsoft account, and identical to what you see in the web app. Connecting from ChatGPT grants nothing extra. Ask an admin for the client grant.
Tools stop working after a day — the access token has a 24 h lifetime. Reconnect the connector; the refresh is silent if you are still signed into Microsoft.

content.text: /donyati-ask — ask an expert
The platform is auto-detected from keywords. To force a platform, pass platform: <slug> in the prompt. Example invocations:

items: /donyati-ask How do you handle intercompany eliminations in OneStream?
/donyati-ask Best Anaplan calculation strategy for a 100M-cell driver model?
/donyati-ask What's the migration path from Hyperion Planning to Oracle EPBCS?
/donyati-ask platform: snowflake — explain Cortex Search vs Cortex Analyst

content.text: /donyati-compare — head-to-head

Each platform's expert analyzes the topic independently — they don't see each other's responses — then a neutral synthesis layer pulls them into a fair comparison. Output is grounded in Donyati's knowledge base, not vendor marketing.

items: /donyati-compare Snowflake vs Databricks for AI/ML workloads
/donyati-compare Anaplan vs Workday Adaptive vs Planful for FP&A
/donyati-compare SAP S/4HANA vs Oracle Fusion ERP for a mid-market manufacturer

content.text: /donyati-summarize — domain-aware summaries

Options: content_type (proposal, sow, assessment, report, general); platform (any platform slug for domain context); output (executive_summary, key_points, action_items, full). Output includes a summary, key points, and platform-specific insights.

items: /donyati-summarize [paste an SOW]
/donyati-summarize [paste a meeting transcript] — output: action_items
/donyati-summarize [paste an assessment report] — content_type: assessment, output: full

content.text: /donyati-knowledge — search the knowledge base

Returns up to 10 matching articles with title, platform/domain, and excerpt. Use these as vetted citations for marketing content, RFP responses, or briefings — they're sourced from Donyati's curated library, not the open web.

items: /donyati-knowledge intercompany eliminations
/donyati-knowledge platform: oracle-epm query: data integration
/donyati-knowledge AIH Tagetik analytics

content.text: /donyati-platforms — list coverage
No arguments. Returns the full live list of platforms with article counts. Use this when you're unsure of the platform slug to pass to /donyati-ask or /donyati-knowledge.
/donyati-setup — verify your key
Run this after receiving a new key, if you suspect your key was rotated, or if MCP tools start failing with auth errors.
/donyati-help — command reference
Shows all commands plus a preview of upcoming Phase 2+ features.
/donyati-demo-assessment — score a vendor demo

Turns a demo transcript into a scorecard against the client's requirement areas — evidence tier and a verified transcript citation behind every score, with what the vendor deferred called out rather than counted as a gap. Pull the transcript in from read.ai first if the demo was a recorded call, or upload it with /donyati-upload.
Examples below use Claude Code slash command syntax. On Desktop / web, swap each slash command for the natural-language phrasing in Section 3B.
Sales / Presales — pitch prep
Scenario: You have a discovery call tomorrow with a manufacturer evaluating Anaplan and Workday Adaptive for FP&A. Workflow:

items: /donyati-platforms — confirm we cover both. Note the slugs (anaplan, workday).
/donyati-compare Anaplan vs Workday Adaptive for mid-market manufacturer FP&A — emphasize sales planning and S&OP integration. Drop highlights into your prep doc.
/donyati-knowledge migration from Excel and Hyperion to Anaplan — pull vetted points for "what does the journey look like" if asked.

content.text: Marketing — fact-checked content
Scenario: You're writing a blog post on AI features in modern FP&A platforms. Workflow:

items: /donyati-knowledge query: predictive forecasting — pull articles across Anaplan PlanIQ, Workday Illuminate, Oracle EPM AI, Planful Predict.
/donyati-ask Compare Anaplan PlanIQ to Workday Illuminate for predictive forecasting — facts only, no marketing language.
/donyati-compare Snowflake Cortex AI vs Databricks AI Functions for embedded ML — generate a comparison table for a sidebar.

content.text: Customer Success — pre-call briefing
Scenario: You have a check-in with a client running Oracle EPBCS. Workflow:

items: /donyati-ask What are common 30-day post-launch issues with EPBCS data integration? — get expert-level talking points anchored in Donyati's experience.
/donyati-summarize [paste last week's meeting transcript] — output: action_items. Confirm what's done before the call.

content.text: Anyone — quick fact-check
Scenario: You're in a conversation, someone makes a claim, you want to verify it. Two seconds, one expert, real answer. No browser tabs.

content.title: Example
content.text: /donyati-ask Does Workday Adaptive support row-level security on plan-input forms?

items: Be specific. "Best Anaplan model design for a 50M-cell workforce planning use case in retail" beats "Anaplan modeling tips." The experts have depth — give them context.
Use /donyati-platforms first if you don't know the slug. Saves a round trip.
Combine commands. Use /donyati-knowledge to find articles, then /donyati-ask to dig into a specific one.
Comparisons need at least 2 platforms. If you say "compare X" with no comparator, the system will pick one for you — usually fine but you have less control.
Don't paste secrets. Anything you send to /donyati-summarize lands in our LLM logs. Same rule as the web app.
Ask follow-ups. Each command is one turn — but Claude is conversational, so you can keep asking. The expert agent doesn't carry state, but Claude (Code, Desktop, or web) does within a conversation.

content.text: Claude Code issues are below. For Desktop / web connector issues, see the troubleshooting bullets at the end of Section 3B.
DONYATI_API_KEY not set

Your shell didn't pick up the export. Check by running: echo $DONYATI_API_KEY. If empty, you either forgot to open a new Terminal window after running the export, used curly quotes, or added it to the wrong file (~/.zshrc vs ~/.bashrc). Re-run the Step 1 line with straight quotes and the right file.
Unauthorized / 401 errors
Three possibilities:

items: Key revoked — ask Matt to issue a new one.
Key has a typo — re-copy from the original message; keys have no spaces.
You're using an old EXPERT_AGENTS_API_KEY — v2 uses DONYATI_API_KEY. Re-run Step 1 with the new name.

content.title: Direct test
content.text: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $DONYATI_API_KEY" https://expert-agents.donyati.com/api/v1/whoami — A working key returns JSON with your key id, name, owner email, and scopes.
/plugin marketplace add fails

If the marketplace add returns an error: check your network (the command clones from GitHub internally), and make sure you're on a recent Claude Code version (the marketplace feature is current as of late 2025). If it still fails, fall back to the MCP-only install in Section 8.
Tool not found

The plugin's MCP server isn't connected. Run /plugin and check the Installed tab. If donyati-expert-agents is listed but tools are missing, run /reload-plugins. If the plugin isn't there, re-run the marketplace install.
Slash commands not showing up

If /donyati-ask doesn't autocomplete, the plugin didn't load. Run /plugin and look at the Installed tab. If donyati-expert-agents isn't there, re-run Step 2 of Section 3. If it's there but commands don't work, run /reload-plugins.
Slow responses

The expert agents call out to OpenRouter; first response can take 5-15 seconds. Subsequent responses are usually faster. If responses consistently take more than 30 seconds, ping Matt — could be a model routing issue.
Rate limit hit
Default is 60 requests/minute per key. If you're getting rate-limited, slow down or ask Matt to bump your limit.

sections.heading: 8. Fallback: MCP-only install in Claude Code (no plugin)

content.text: If the marketplace install in Section 3 gives you trouble, you can install just the MCP server in Claude Code. You'll get all eight tools but lose the /donyati-* slash command shortcuts — you'll need to call the tools by their MCP names (e.g., ask Claude Code "use the consult tool to ask…").

content.title: Run in Terminal
content.text: claude mcp add --transport http expert-agents https://expert-agents.donyati.com/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $DONYATI_API_KEY"
Verify with claude mcp list — you should see expert-agents in the list. Open Claude Code and ask it to list available MCP tools.
Note: For Claude Desktop / claude.ai web there's no plugin to begin with — the Custom Connector + SSO setup in Section 3B is the standard path, not a fallback.

content.title: Important
content.text: Treat the plugin like the web app. Anything you send is logged for billing, audit, and may land in the knowledge base. Don't paste anything you wouldn't paste into the web app.

items: API keys are scoped to you. Each teammate gets a unique key. Don't share them.
Desktop / web sign-ins are tied to your Azure AD identity. The connector's access dies if your Donyati account is deactivated.
Requests are logged. Admins can see per-user / per-key usage at /admin/api-usage.
Content you summarize/ingest is stored. Future ingest commands will stamp your owner email on every row.
Per-org scoping coming in Phase 5. For now every authenticated user has full read access. If your role shouldn't see all clients, hold ingest/summarize work until per-org scopes ship.

sections.heading: 12. Plugin reach — what is web-only, and why

content.text: Not everything in the Expert Agents web app is meant to be reachable from Claude. Some of it is held back on purpose; some of it is a gap somebody is tracking. Without that written down the two look identical from the connector — you ask for a client's contacts, nothing happens, and you cannot tell whether that is a bug worth reporting. This table covers the features shipped between 20 August and 4 September 2026, measured against the connector on 2026-09-07.

rows: Deliberate. The contacts design puts /v1 sync and an MCP tool in Phase 3, blocked on a field-level precedence table being implemented first. Until an external writer knows which system wins per field, a connector write would silently overwrite a curated contact.
A tracked gap, not a decision: AB#6083 covers reference search on /v1 and MCP.
Closed since this was reported. Pass a pocSlug or a projectId and it walks the funnel behind and ahead of it, including a conversion later undone.
On MCP as propose_assessment; not on the /v1 REST API

Split on purpose. Drafting and listing are conversational work. Pushing a proposal makes it client-facing and withdrawing takes it back from respondents mid-flight; both stay signed-in acts. The missing /v1 route is a gap under AB#6104.
Partly — list_pocs returns spend to a caller holding the cost permissions
Reading is reachable and gated. Administering it is not: attributing a resource to a POC rewrites the cost map for every reader of it.
Deliberate. The action creates an engagement row and generates a client SOW against it. A one-shot connector call that creates a client record as a side effect is the wrong shape for it.

content.title: What web-only costs you
content.text: Every row marked web-only means a consultant working in Claude has to open a browser to finish the job. That cost is accepted for specific reasons — a write that could overwrite curated data, an act that reaches the client, or a side effect that creates records. It is not a general position that the connector is a read-only surface.
